purpose: Cross-brand evidence for separating observed battery behaviour from raw capacity. Values from unlike protocols must never be averaged directly.
caveat: Capacity-normalized drain is an observed system result, not a pure software coefficient. SoC, display, modem, thermal policy, battery voltage/usable window and test protocol remain confounders until controlled by later model stages.

sources.name: GSMArena
sources.protocol: Active Use battery tests with separate web, video and gaming runtimes

sources.name: Notebookcheck
sources.protocol: Wi-Fi browsing/video/load tests, generally display-normalized around 150 cd/m² for practical battery tests

sources.name: Tom's Guide
sources.protocol: Web surfing battery test, generally 150 nits; some older OnePlus 13 result used an earlier test version

sources.name: PhoneArena
sources.protocol: Separate browsing, video streaming and 3D gaming lab tests

tomsguide.protocolNote: Reported by Tom's Guide as produced under an older version of its test.

phonearena.variantNote: PhoneArena entry reports 6000 mAh; do not combine with 5410 mAh global-unit results without variant control.

initialFindings: The same device can rank very differently across protocols, proving that protocol identity must be a first-class field.
The iPhone 17 Pro Max shows unusually low capacity-normalized GSMArena web/video drain despite its smaller battery, making it a strong residual-analysis candidate.

Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra performs very strongly in Notebookcheck and Tom's Guide web-style tests despite 5000 mAh, but less strongly in GSMArena web, reinforcing the need for protocol-specific coefficients.
Pixel 10 Pro XL repeatedly shows weak heavy/gaming endurance relative to capacity in GSMArena and PhoneArena, so one global software multiplier would be misleading.
OnePlus 13 benefits materially from 6000 mAh capacity, but its gaming efficiency is less impressive than its web/video endurance.
Xiaomi 15 Ultra, vivo X200 Pro and Oppo Find X8 Pro show that large Si/C batteries alone do not explain ranking; workload behaviour differs substantially.
